name: read_presentation_context
description: Read the current presentation file, slide inventory, selection and template context in one call. Returns title, slide_count, slide_width_points / slide_height_points, is_default_theme, has_content, theme_palette, theme_fonts, template_body_font_pt, content_language, display_language, masters (layouts with ids), slides_metadata (1-based position to stable slide id), the selection and a structure_fingerprint. Optional template or selection failures do not discard the file inventory. The fingerprint tracks slide and shape IDs, not the title, text or styling.

name: list_slide_shapes
description: Lists every shape on one slide with its ref, name, type, position and text (text cut after 400 characters). read_slide_text and edit_slide_text take only a `ref` from this list; a ref names the slide and the shape together, so the two cannot get out of step.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: edit_slide_chart
description: Changes an existing chart, or builds a chart form that create_slide_chart does not offer (combo, 3D, pie, secondary axis), by editing its OOXML directly; also the tool for small, exact XML changes to a chart. A new chart of a standard form goes through create_slide_chart. Never draw a chart out of geometric shapes.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

code.description: Body of an async function with zip (a JSZip archive) and markDirty already in scope: write the statements directly; do not wrap them in a function such as async ({ zip, markDirty }) => { ... }, which is defined but never called, so nothing is written. The exported slide is always ppt/slides/slide1.xml regardless of slide id. The package holds only this slide: media, charts and layouts of other slides are not reachable. After a package replacement the slide id changes; follow the returned id mapping and call list_slide_shapes again before further edits. Read a part with await zip.file(path).async("string"), write it with zip.file(path, xml), and call markDirty() or the edit is discarded; code may also only read and return data. escapeXml(text) escapes text embedded in XML; a bare & silently drops every following run. Two chart helpers are in scope too: buildChart(spec) gives the chart XML the builder would write, and insertChart(zip, spec) adds a complete built chart to the package.

autosize_shape_ids.description: cNvPr ids of the shapes whose text body you changed. A shape set to AutoSizeShapeToFitText gets that setting applied again once the slide is back in the deck, so PowerPoint works out its size before verify_slides measures it; a shape with another autoSize setting is left as it is. For a table, every row.height is written back with its own value, which makes PowerPoint lay out the frame again (a font change alone does not resize the drawn table). Leave it out when only non-text content changed (positions, fills, pictures).

name: create_slide_chart
description:
Builds a chart on a slide from a spec; this is the normal way to add a chart. The chart XML comes from templates that already follow the house chart standard (no legend, value axis removed on bar forms, emphasis through the accent, units inside number formats), which is quicker and safer than writing chart OOXML by hand. Forms: column, bar (horizontal), line, slope, stacked column with totals, Likert (a 100% stacked bar), waterfall, scatter and big number. The result is an ordinary native chart: change it later with edit_built_chart and a complete spec, or with edit_slide_chart for exact XML edits. Any other form, or finer changes, go through edit_slide_chart.

- Give the form, the categories, the raw values, a number format holding the whole unit (on stacked forms the totals format holds the unit and the segment values stay plain), the index of the single category or point that carries the message, and a style.
- Always give a style: on a templated deck the accent from theme_palette, on a blank deck the accent you put in the master, plus the deck's body font and its neutral colours.
- When the deck has a chart standard, first run read_chart_style on a slide that holds one of its charts and pass what it returns as style and construction; pass a title when the deck's charts have native titles. Do not guess fonts or colours.
- On a line chart, choose series[].point_labels to suit the story and the room available, and mark forecast periods with forecast_from. growth_arrows draws straight arrows from bar to bar; elbow arrows and difference markers are drawn with edit_slide_xml.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

spec.description: The chart as data: choose its form, give raw values and display formats, and the builder writes chart XML that follows the house standard, with no OOXML on your side. A field listed under properties applies to each form that names it.

position.description: Where the chart frame goes, in EMU; leave it out for the default frame that fills the slide

style.description: The chart's colours and font. Pass the deck's accent and fonts so the chart matches the deck; a value left out falls back to the house palette (blue accent, greys, Calibri), which only suits the untouched default theme

accent.description: The one emphasis color; the deck's accent (theme_palette.accent1, or the accent set in the master)

negative.description: Waterfall decreases; defaults to a warm orange

neutral.description: Colour of the bars and lines that are not accented; mid grey when omitted

totals.description: Colour of waterfall totals and their labels; dark grey when omitted

text.description: Label and axis text; defaults to near-black

text_secondary.description: Axis titles, subtitles; defaults to dark gray

bg.description: The colour of the slide behind the chart, which also fills the growth-arrow labels and the forecast hatching; give it whenever the background is not white

ramp.description: Neutral shades from dark to light, for Likert and stacked segments

font.description: The font of all chart text; normally the deck's body font

construction.description: How the chart is put together. Leave it out for the house standard. When the deck has its own chart standard, read one of its charts and set these to match (legend position, value axis shown or not, gridlines); a title inside the chart goes in the top-level `title`

value_axis.description: Removed on bar forms by the house standard; line and scatter charts keep theirs

gridlines.description: Horizontal value gridlines; house default off

point_labels.description: Custom label text for specific points, e.g. [{index: 0, text: '16.3 万辆'}]. index is against categories/values in the caller's display order (same convention as categories), regardless of the builder's internal bottom-up storage order for a horizontal bar chart. Overrides the auto value label (number_format) only for the listed points; other points keep the default value label.

title.description: Native chart title, optional. The house standard has none (leave it out and the title area stays empty); set one only when the chart really needs a heading of its own

subtitle.description: The chart's descriptive label, as a second line under title, worded as the charts skill says

values.description: Bars start at zero, so values are zero or more; a comparison with both signs needs another form

accent_index.description: Index of the single category carrying the message; every other category is drawn in the neutral grey

number_format.description: OOXML formatCode. Put the whole unit in it, prefix and suffix, so each data label shows it: '"$"#,##0"M"' gives $42M, '0"%"' gives 38%, '#,##0" people"' gives 1,240 people. With a plain "#,##0" the reader has to guess the unit

forecast_from.description: Index (0-based) of the first forecast category. Bars from there on are hatched (a diagonal pattern in the same colours) so they read as estimates, not actuals. Add 'E' to the labels of those categories as well

label.description: The change, signed and with its unit, such as '+21%'

from.description: Index of the category where the arrow starts; by default the arrow's own position in the list

to.description: Index of the category where the arrow ends; by default from + 1

growth_arrows.description: Straight arrows drawn over the chart from the top of one bar to the top of another, each with its change figure centred on the line (on a patch of slide background that covers the arrow behind it). Each arrow is one item, such as {from: 0, to: 1, label: '+21%'} between neighbouring bars and {from: 0, to: N-1, label: '+38%'} from the first bar to the last. Use arrows only for changes that matter

accent_point_index.description: The single point carrying the message, if there is one

name: read_chart_style
description: Reads each native chart on a slide and gives back its style in the fields of create_slide_chart's spec: the form (the spec's type, such as column, bar or line), fonts (or font_inherits_theme), the fill hexes and scheme colours set on it, legend position, whether the value axis shows, gridlines, native title, data label position, gap width, and whatever the builder cannot reproduce (combo, 3D, pie, secondary axis). When the deck has a chart standard, call it before create_slide_chart instead of reading raw XML, and hand its result to create_slide_chart as style and construction, which makes the new chart match.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: edit_slide_master
description: Edits the slide master and its layouts through OOXML: backgrounds, decoration (accent lines, dividers, borders), brand shapes, fonts, theme colours and placeholders. Use it for anything that should show on every slide, and for theme, rebrand and deck-wide layout work. The edited package comes in with a theme name of its own and each slide moves to the new layout with the same name; the result lists slides whose layout was ambiguous or missing, and whether the old master stayed because it could not be removed.

code.description: Body of an async function with zip (a JSZip archive) and markDirty already in scope: write the statements directly; do not wrap them in a function such as async ({ zip, markDirty }) => { ... }, which is defined but never called, so nothing is written. The package holds the exported first slide and its structure; master and theme parts are ppt/slideMasters/slideMaster1.xml, ppt/slideLayouts/slideLayoutN.xml and ppt/theme/theme1.xml. Read a part with await zip.file(path).async("string"), write it with zip.file(path, xml), and call markDirty() or the edit is discarded; code may also only read and return data. escapeXml(text) escapes text embedded in XML; a bare & silently drops every following run.

name: read_slide_text
description:
Returns the paragraphs of a shape's text body as raw OOXML (the <a:p> elements, DrawingML prefix a:), so you can see the text with its formatting, bullets and styles before you change it. Change existing text with edit_slide_text, edit_slide_xml or find_and_replace; an update_shape with text in presentation_apply_patch drops run formatting, so keep that for text you wrote yourself.

What the XML holds:
- <a:p> a paragraph, <a:r> a run, <a:t> its characters
- <a:pPr> paragraph settings: algn="l|ctr|r|just", lvl (indent level, from 0), marL/indent, <a:lnSpc>/<a:spcBef>/<a:spcAft> each holding <a:spcPts val="1400"/> (in hundredths of a point)
- bullets, set in <a:pPr>: <a:buChar char="•"/>, <a:buAutoNum type="arabicPeriod"/>, <a:buNone/>, <a:buFont typeface="Arial"/>
- <a:rPr> run settings: sz (in hundredths of a point; sz="1600" is 16 pt), b="1", i="1", u="sng", lang, baseline; <a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2"/> marks a link
- colour: <a:solidFill><a:schemeClr val="tx2"/></a:solidFill> from the theme, or <a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="FF0000"/></a:solidFill> fixed
- <a:latin typeface="Calibri"/> a font set on the run itself

ref.description: A shape's ref as list_slide_shapes gave it (such as "258:5"). It names the slide and the shape together; pass back refs you were given and never build one yourself.

name: read_slide_image
description: Render one slide as a PNG for visual inspection. Use slide IDs returned by read_presentation_context.

width.description: PNG width in pixels. Defaults to 960.

height.description: PNG height in pixels. Defaults to 540 on a 16:9 slide (the slide's aspect ratio at the width).

name: edit_slide_text
description:
Replaces the paragraphs of a shape with <a:p> XML you supply. The shape keeps its <a:bodyPr> and <a:lstStyle>, but the formatting of single runs is not kept: it sits in each run's <a:rPr>, inside the paragraphs being replaced. When the shape's <a:lstStyle> is empty (the usual case), a new run without <a:rPr> takes the layout or master default, not the old run's colour, size or font. Read the shape with read_slide_text first.

How to write paragraph XML (here or in edit_slide_xml):
- Nothing in OOXML is implied: take <a:pPr> and <a:rPr> unchanged from what you read and alter only what the user asked for; dropping b="1" turns bold off.
- Leave <a:schemeClr> where it is; a hex value in its place cuts the text off from the theme.
- Add <a:latin> only when the user wants a particular font; otherwise the text follows the theme fonts.
- Set lang on <a:rPr> to the text's language (zh-CN for Chinese, en-US for English) or leave it out; en-US is never a default to impose.
- A bullet is <a:buChar> in <a:pPr>, never a "•" typed into the text. First-level bullets have lvl="0" or no lvl; second-level bullets have lvl="1". A heading line stays at level 0 and gets <a:buNone/>; it is not a level of its own.
- Bullet indent: in a body placeholder leave marL and indent unset so the master's values apply. In a text box you added, take the master's first-level values, and only when those are unknown use marL="228600" indent="-228600". When adding to a list, reuse the values it already has.
- A footnote mark is <a:rPr baseline="30000"/>.
- Titles align as their layout says: Title Slide and Section Header layouts centre them, content layouts align them left. A template's own placeholder alignment takes precedence.

A first-level bullet; ordinary bullets take neither <a:buNone/> nor lvl="1":
<a:p><a:pPr><a:buFont typeface="Arial"/><a:buChar char="•"/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr sz="1600"/><a:t>Bullet text</a:t></a:r></a:p>

A heading line without a bullet:
<a:p><a:pPr><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr sz="1600" b="1"/><a:t>Header text</a:t></a:r></a:p>

ref.description: A shape's ref as list_slide_shapes gave it (such as "258:5"). It names the slide and the shape together; pass back refs you were given and never build one yourself.

code.description: The new paragraphs as raw OOXML <a:p> elements, which take the place of the shape's text

name: edit_slide_xml
description:
Edit raw OOXML of a slide for what the other slide tools cannot express: existing table cell text, precise run formatting, grouping, custom XML manipulation. Two or more text edits on one slide go in one call.

- Coordinates are EMU (12700 per point).
- Preserve <a:bodyPr> and <a:lstStyle> when replacing a <p:txBody>; paragraph XML follows the rules in edit_slide_text.
- Table cell text lives in <a:tbl>/<a:tr>/<a:tc>. Table height derives from rows and content; <a:ext cy> writes are ignored, so shorten copy or reduce cell fonts and pass the table id in autosize_shape_ids.
- Recolouring an existing SVG icon means editing the SVG in ppt/media/ through its <asvg:svgBlip r:embed> relationship; setting the shape fill colours the box behind it.

name: verify_slides
description: Checks slides for shapes that may overlap, shapes outside the slide and text with low contrast. Gives results per slide, each with a `slideId`, and states what it covered in `total_slides`, `from_slide` and `to_slide`. When a shape's text colour falls short of WCAG AA (4.5:1) against the shape's own solid fill, the slide's `contrast_warnings` lists `{shape_id, shape_name, font_color, bg_color, ratio, msg}`; look at each and repair the real defects before you call the slide finished. To read or change a flagged shape's text, get its ref from list_slide_shapes for that slideId. On a long deck pass a range (0-based indexes, one below the 1-based position in slides_metadata: `{from_slide: 0, to_slide: 19}` covers slides 1 to 20) so the result is not cut short; a result with `to_slide < total_slides - 1` means slides are left, so call again from the next one. A measured overlap stays a candidate until you have seen it, since deliberate layering overlaps too.

from_slide.description: 0-based index of the first slide (the slides_metadata position minus 1). Defaults to 0 (first slide).

to_slide.description: 0-based index of the last slide, inclusive (the slides_metadata position minus 1). Defaults to from_slide + 19 (a page of 20 slides); the result's to_slide says where it stopped.

name: verify_slide_visual
description: Independent visual review of one slide. Captures a fresh render of the slide and its measured geometry; a separate reviewer that sees nothing of this conversation checks them against an objective defect list (overlaps, overflow, collisions, accidental sibling inconsistency, off-centre badge numbers, unreadable text, low contrast, detached connectors, leftover placeholders). List what you changed in expected_changes so the review also confirms each change or reports it NOT VISIBLE. Returns verdict done or needs_work with the defects to repair, and the render it reviewed.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or a patch result.

expected_changes.description: One line per change you made on this slide.

name: find_and_replace
description:
Replaces text throughout the deck in a single call. Use it for every bulk change of wording (renames, rebrands, changed terms) instead of editing shapes one by one with edit_slide_text or edit_slide_xml. It works on the OOXML and reaches every text run in every shape (shapes in groups and placeholders as well), in tables and in speaker notes.

Formatting stays: a match within a single run keeps the formatting of that run, and a match spread over several runs (say a word split by a formatting change or a spelling mark) takes the formatting of its first run. The result gives the number of replacements in total and per pair, where they happened on each slide (shape, table cell, notes), and what was skipped and why. Left unchanged and reported as skipped: generated fields, chart and SmartArt text, and text on layouts or the master (change those with edit_slide_master). A match that crosses a line break is reported as skipped, not replaced. To see how many matches there are before changing anything, run it with dry_run:true first.

find.description: The text to look for, as plain text (no regular expressions).

replace.description: The new text, in its plain casing (see preserve_case). Empty removes the found text.

pairs.description: Pairs of find and replace, applied one after another: each pair works on the text the pair before it left.

match.description: "whole_word" (the default) matches only where no ASCII letter or digit touches the term, so replacing "form" does not change "information". "substring" matches inside longer words as well.

case_sensitive.description: false by default: matches ignore case.

preserve_case.description: false by default: each match becomes the replacement exactly as written. When true, each match keeps the casing pattern it had (all capitals, an initial capital, or all lower case); replacing Atlasware with Novagrid makes ATLASWARE become NOVAGRID and atlasware become novagrid.

slide_ids.description: Only these slides. Leave the field out to cover every slide (an empty list is refused, not read as the whole deck).

include_notes.description: true by default: speaker notes are searched and changed with the slide text.

dry_run.description: false by default. When true, only counts the matches and lists where they are on each slide, changing nothing.

name: presentation_apply_patch
description:
Compose or revise 1-3 slides as typed native presentation objects (the default way to build a page). Give each page a slide_ref and an ordered list of operations in points; the executor enforces the design rules that hand-written scripts get wrong: text roles carry font presets and minimum sizes (body >= 14 pt), colors/fonts resolve from design_system tokens so every page shares one palette, and text on a shape goes into the shape's own frame so badges and labels are centred. Pass the latest structure_fingerprint (from read_presentation_context or the previous patch's structure_fingerprint_after); a stale fingerprint is rejected before any mutation. This tool never produces HTML or an intermediate PPTX.

1. Design system first. On the first patch of a new or restyled deck, declare design_system once: colour tokens (add accent2, line, code_bg as needed) and fonts.heading / fonts.body. On a templated deck take them from theme_palette and theme_fonts; for a requested rebrand derive them from the supplied reference. Register the whole background, card, text and accent relationship; never keep an old background palette and swap in new accents. Later patches reference colours by token so pages cannot drift; a palette change is one coherent new design_system, not per-shape hex edits.
2. Roles, not sizes. Give every text a role: title, subtitle, section (small eyebrow label), body, label, caption, footnote, badge (a number or short word centred in a shape), number (a hero figure) or code. Roles carry size, weight, alignment and margins and have accessibility floors; a font_size under a role's floor is rejected, so trim copy or enlarge the container instead. Choose sizes from the slide-design hierarchy; for a template body size under the body floor, omit the role and set text_style.font_size.
3. Text on a shape goes in the shape. Badges, step numbers, chips and labelled boxes are one add_shape with text and role "badge" or "label". Never stack an add_text on a shape to fake centring.
4. Repeat with identical values. Siblings use the same width, height, role, fill token and spacing, computed from one grid (for example three 252 pt columns with 34 pt gutters starting at 48 pt) and reused verbatim wherever the pattern repeats.
5. Layouts and placeholders. Prefer a real layout_id over Blank, and rotate layouts across the deck. On a freshly created slide set clear_existing_shapes: true only when your composition replaces every placeholder, never on a page with user content. Fill or delete every placeholder on a slide you just added; empty placeholders still render. Delete placeholders only on slides you added, since text in a placeholder of an existing slide belongs to the user. A direct user request to remove a specific placeholder is still honoured. Measure the title band before placing content under it: list_slide_shapes on the new slide, then read the title placeholder's top + height; title bands vary between templates. To move an existing slide onto another layout, give its slide_id with the new layout_id.
6. One slide per patch while building. Each result returns slides[].slide_id, every created shape's shape_id and ref, and structure_fingerprint_after; pass that fingerprint as the next patch's base_structure_fingerprint instead of re-reading. Fix a page with update_shape / delete_shape on the returned ids, not by rebuilding it. Several slides in one patch are fine for slide deletes, reorders or one identical change across slides. Delete or reorder with {"slide_ref": "S4", "slide_id": <id>, "delete_slide": true} or {"slide_ref": "S2", "slide_id": <id>, "move_to": 1}; slide-level changes run after the content edits in the patch.
7. Images and charts. Publish an image with publish_office_asset, list its descriptor under assets with a short key, and place it with add_image. Charts are not operations here: leave their space in the patch and create them with create_slide_chart.
8. Canvas. Every operation stays inside the slide size. Set explicit left and top on every shape.
9. Containers fit their content. Size a card or bar to its text plus 16 to 24 pt of padding; text sitting on a shape is inset 10 to 15 pt from its edges. Fill the page with content, larger type within the hierarchy or wider gutters, never by stretching empty containers. Stacked layers share one left edge unless the stagger carries meaning.
10. Stacking. Operations stack in the order listed; list background shapes first, and fix an existing shape's stacking with update_shape z_order.
11. Connectors and diagrams. Diagram slides (process flows, timelines, cycles, org charts) are built here: add_shape nodes with label or badge text, add_connector with end_arrow between them, all on one grid. For every node-to-node link set start_anchor and end_anchor and pick the edge (left, right, top, bottom); normally omit offset for the midpoint (use 0.15 to 0.85 only to separate parallel ports; never a rounded corner). Straight is a direct relation; Elbow is a simple orthogonal one. A feedback loop or a route that must avoid objects is one logical Straight connector with waypoints. Never fake one route with several arrowed connectors, separate triangles or hairline rectangles. Raw left/top/width/height is only for a free-floating line. To repair a connector, delete_shape it and add an anchored one in the same patch; after moving a node, recreate its routes.
12. Tables. add_table already applies the slide-table style; mark the message with highlight_rows or highlight_columns, and use table_style "host_default" only when matching a deck whose tables use the presentation app's built-in style. Size before inserting: a single-line row is about 30 pt, a two-line row about 50 pt; compute what fits and split rather than run off the slide. Cells over about 40 words belong in a text box or footnote instead. Restyle an existing table with update_table.

design_system.description: Design tokens declared once for the deck and remembered for later patches in this session. Colors are referenced by token name anywhere a color is accepted; fonts by heading/body/mono. Declare at least accent, text, muted, bg and card.

slide_ref.description: Your stable label for this page (e.g. S3). Echoed in the result.

slide_id.description: Current slide id to edit an existing page. Omit to create a new slide.

layout_id.description: A layout id from read_presentation_context.masters (prefer a real layout over Blank). On a new slide it picks the layout; with slide_id it re-applies that layout to the existing slide (alone, or before this slide's operations). Then call list_slide_shapes: the slide's placeholders follow the new layout.

slide_master_id.description: The master that owns layout_id; needed only when the same layout id exists under more than one master.

position.description: New slides only: 1-based position, counted before this patch deletes any slide. Use move_to for an existing slide.

background.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

clear_existing_shapes.description: New slides only: delete the layout placeholders the new slide inherited before applying operations. Rejected when slide_id targets an existing page; use delete_shape for specific shapes there.

delete_slide.description: Existing slides only (slide_id required): delete the whole slide. Give no operations, background, layout_id or move_to with it. Runs after every other change in the patch; the deck must keep at least one slide.

move_to.description: Existing slides only (slide_id required): final 1-based position of this slide. May be combined with operations on the same slide, or used alone (omit operations) for a pure reorder, which needs no new visual review.

items.description: One native operation. add_text: a text box (role + text). add_shape: a geometric shape; when it carries text the text lives in the shape's own frame and is centred (use role "badge" for numbers/short labels). add_connector: a deterministic native OOXML connector or routed sequence of connector segments, optionally with one native terminal arrowhead. For node-to-node diagrams use start_anchor/end_anchor so the executor resolves visible edge points; use raw left/top/width/height only for free-floating lines. add_image: an image-filled rectangle from assets[].key. add_table: a native table from string values, styled as a slide table by default (bold header without fill, rules between rows only, bold first column, numeric columns right-aligned). update_table: restyle an existing native table by shape_id (cell ranges, row rules, row height, column widths). update_shape / delete_shape: existing shape ids from list_slide_shapes or a previous patch result.

name.description: Stable readable shape name, e.g. card2-title. Reported back with the created shape id.

text.description: Required for add_text; optional on add_shape (rendered inside the shape) and update_shape (replaces the text; run formatting is reset). Use \n for a line/paragraph break inside multi-line text (e.g. an analysis card's bullet lines) — it is rendered as a real paragraph break, not a literal backslash-n.

role.description: Typography preset. Sizes/floors in pt: title 32/28, subtitle 18/16, section 12/11, body 16/14, label 14/12, caption 12/11, footnote 10/9, badge 16/12 (centred, no wrap, zero margins), number 28/20, code 14/12 (mono font).

text_style.description: Explicit overrides on top of the role preset. Omit fields you do not need; a font_size below the role floor is rejected. On update_shape only the stated fields change: alignment, margins, wrap and autosize are kept, so recolouring a badge never un-centres it.

font_name.description: Font name or a design_system font token: heading, body, mono; a token needs design_system.fonts to declare it.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

shape_id.description: Required for update_shape, update_table and delete_shape.

connector_type.description: add_connector only; default Straight. With semantic anchors, Elbow is rendered as a deterministic orthogonal route instead of host auto-routing. Explicit waypoint routes must use Straight because every route leg is a straight native segment.

end_arrow.description: add_connector only: add one native OOXML triangle line-ending at the final route endpoint. Intermediate route segments never receive arrowheads.

start_anchor.description: Required for node-to-node add_connector operations. Identify the source by shape_name when it is created in this patch, or shape_id when it already exists on the slide. Must be paired with end_anchor and cannot be mixed with raw geometry.

shape_name.description: Stable name of a geometry-owning shape created anywhere in this same slide patch.

shape_id.description: Existing live shape id from list_slide_shapes or a previous presentation_apply_patch result.

offset.description: Position along the edge, default 0.5. The safe range avoids transparent rounded corners; keep 0.5 for non-rectangular shapes.

end_anchor.description: Required for node-to-node add_connector operations. Identify the destination by shape_name when it is created in this patch, or shape_id when it already exists on the slide. Must be paired with start_anchor and cannot be mixed with raw geometry.

shape_name.description: Stable name of a geometry-owning shape created anywhere in this same slide patch.

shape_id.description: Existing live shape id from list_slide_shapes or a previous presentation_apply_patch result.

offset.description: Position along the edge, default 0.5. The safe range avoids transparent rounded corners; keep 0.5 for non-rectangular shapes.

waypoints.description: Optional intermediate route points for one logical connector. Requires start_anchor/end_anchor and connector_type Straight. The executor creates contiguous straight segments and puts end_arrow only on the final segment.

values.description: add_table only: rows of cell strings; the first row is the header when header_row is true (default).

header_fill.description: add_table only: header fill colour (hex or design_system token). Omit for the default unfilled bold header.

header_color.description: add_table only: header text colour (hex or token).

font_size.description: add_table only: cell font size, default 14.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

z_order.description: update_shape only: move the shape in the slide's stacking order.

color.description: 6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a color token declared in design_system.colors of this or an earlier patch; undeclared tokens are rejected.
6-digit hex color (with or without #) or a design_system color token such as "accent".

left.description: Points from the slide's left edge.

top.description: Points from the slide's top edge.

width.description: Points. At least 0.1 for shapes. In raw add_connector geometry, 0 makes a vertical line and a negative value points left. Omit when using semantic anchors.

height.description: Points. At least 0.1 for shapes. In raw add_connector geometry, 0 makes a horizontal line and a negative value points up. Omit when using semantic anchors.

table_style.description: add_table only. minimal (default): no fills, thin rules between rows, no column borders. host_default: keep the presentation app's built-in table style.

rule_color.description: add_table only: colour of the rules between rows (hex or token); default the design_system line token, else light grey.

rule_weight.description: add_table only: rule weight in points, default 1.

first_column_bold.description: add_table only: bold row labels in the first column, default true.

highlight_rows.description: add_table only: 1-based table rows (the header is row 1) that carry the message; they get a light tint of highlight_fill.

highlight_columns.description: add_table only: 1-based columns that carry the message; tinted like highlight_rows.

highlight_fill.description: add_table only: tint colour for highlighted rows or columns, default the accent token (a 15% tint of it over white).

column_widths.description: add_table / update_table: one width in points per column.

row_height.description: add_table / update_table: height in points for every row; text that needs more space still grows the row.

cell_styles.description: update_table only: style changes for 1-based cell ranges. Text stays unchanged; change cell text with edit_slide_xml.

fill.description: Hex, token, or "none" to remove the fill.

row_rules.description: update_table only: replace the table's borders with thin rules between rows and no column borders.

assets.description: Image descriptors returned by publish_office_asset, each with a short key referenced by add_image.asset_key.

name: edit_built_chart
description: Swaps the content of an existing chart for a new spec while the chart object stays the same (its position, relationship and shape id). It changes a chart's data, form or style without raw XML: run read_chart_style first, then pass a complete spec that includes the style and construction it returned. A chart of a form the builder cannot draw (combo, 3D, secondary axis, pie) is refused; edit its XML with edit_slide_chart.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

spec.description: The chart as data: choose its form, give raw values and display formats, and the builder writes chart XML that follows the house standard, with no OOXML on your side. A field listed under properties applies to each form that names it.

position.description: Where the chart frame goes, in EMU; leave it out for the default frame that fills the slide

style.description: The chart's colours and font. Pass the deck's accent and fonts so the chart matches the deck; a value left out falls back to the house palette (blue accent, greys, Calibri), which only suits the untouched default theme

accent.description: The one emphasis color; the deck's accent (theme_palette.accent1, or the accent set in the master)

negative.description: Waterfall decreases; defaults to a warm orange

neutral.description: Colour of the bars and lines that are not accented; mid grey when omitted

totals.description: Colour of waterfall totals and their labels; dark grey when omitted

text.description: Label and axis text; defaults to near-black

text_secondary.description: Axis titles, subtitles; defaults to dark gray

bg.description: The colour of the slide behind the chart, which also fills the growth-arrow labels and the forecast hatching; give it whenever the background is not white

ramp.description: Neutral shades from dark to light, for Likert and stacked segments

font.description: The font of all chart text; normally the deck's body font

construction.description: How the chart is put together. Leave it out for the house standard. When the deck has its own chart standard, read one of its charts and set these to match (legend position, value axis shown or not, gridlines); a title inside the chart goes in the top-level `title`

value_axis.description: Removed on bar forms by the house standard; line and scatter charts keep theirs

gridlines.description: Horizontal value gridlines; house default off

point_labels.description: Custom label text for specific points, e.g. [{index: 0, text: '16.3 万辆'}]. index is against categories/values in the caller's display order (same convention as categories), regardless of the builder's internal bottom-up storage order for a horizontal bar chart. Overrides the auto value label (number_format) only for the listed points; other points keep the default value label.

title.description: Native chart title, optional. The house standard has none (leave it out and the title area stays empty); set one only when the chart really needs a heading of its own

subtitle.description: The chart's descriptive label, as a second line under title, worded as the charts skill says

values.description: Bars start at zero, so values are zero or more; a comparison with both signs needs another form

accent_index.description: Index of the single category carrying the message; every other category is drawn in the neutral grey

number_format.description: OOXML formatCode. Put the whole unit in it, prefix and suffix, so each data label shows it: '"$"#,##0"M"' gives $42M, '0"%"' gives 38%, '#,##0" people"' gives 1,240 people. With a plain "#,##0" the reader has to guess the unit

forecast_from.description: Index (0-based) of the first forecast category. Bars from there on are hatched (a diagonal pattern in the same colours) so they read as estimates, not actuals. Add 'E' to the labels of those categories as well

label.description: The change, signed and with its unit, such as '+21%'

from.description: Index of the category where the arrow starts; by default the arrow's own position in the list

to.description: Index of the category where the arrow ends; by default from + 1

growth_arrows.description: Straight arrows drawn over the chart from the top of one bar to the top of another, each with its change figure centred on the line (on a patch of slide background that covers the arrow behind it). Each arrow is one item, such as {from: 0, to: 1, label: '+21%'} between neighbouring bars and {from: 0, to: N-1, label: '+38%'} from the first bar to the last. Use arrows only for changes that matter

name: duplicate_slide
description: Copies a slide and puts the copy directly after it. Returns the copy's slide_id and source_slide_id. It reproduces the slide with its native content as it stands; to design a new slide use presentation_apply_patch.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

name: import_slides
description: Insert slides from a .pptx the user supplied (a template, a colleague's pages, a reference deck) into this presentation as native slides. The chosen slides keep their source order and land after after_slide_id (default: after the last slide). Returns each source position with its new slide_id; fill or delete their placeholders and verify them like any new slide. Use duplicate_slide to copy a slide of this deck. With keep_source_formatting the deck's original theme stays primary until you move slides onto the imported master or rebuild the theme with edit_slide_master.

asset.description: The .pptx descriptor returned by publish_office_asset (purpose input_pptx), passed unchanged.

source_positions.description: 1-based positions of the slides to import from the source deck. Omit to import every slide.

after_slide_id.description: Current slide id from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata; the imported slides are inserted after it. Omit to append at the end.

formatting.description: use_destination_theme (default) adopts this deck's master; keep_source_formatting keeps the source look and adds its master.

name: copy_image_between_slides
description: Copies a picture from one slide to another, bringing its media files and relationships to the target slide so it shows there, with its crop, filters and alt text. Do not copy a <p:pic> with edit_slide_xml: the one-slide package holds none of the other slide's media, so its r:embed would point nowhere.

from_slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

from_shape_id.description: The cNvPr id of the <p:pic> to copy, the `id` that list_slide_shapes gives.

to_slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

x.description: Left edge in points; leave it out to keep the source position.

y.description: Top edge in points; leave it out to keep the source position.

width.description: Width in points; leave it out to keep the source size.

height.description: Height in points; leave it out to keep the source size.

name: insert_icon
description: Place an icon from the bundled set on a slide as a native vector picture (SVG, with a PNG fallback for old readers) in one colour. Get the icon name from search_icons first. Returns the new picture's ref. Icons mark three to six parallel items: one per item, beside its label, with the same size, style and colour across the slide. Never use emoji in their place. To change a placed icon's colour, insert it again in the new colour and delete the old picture.

slide_id.description: Slide ID from read_presentation_context.slides_metadata[].slide_id or verify_slides output.

style.description: regular (outline; the default) or filled. Keep one style on a slide.

size.description: Width and height in points (icons are square); 48 when omitted. 24 to 48 pt suits an icon next to a label.

color.description: #RRGGBB, normally the deck's accent or text colour from read_presentation_context.theme_palette; black when omitted.

alt_text.description: What the icon stands for, read out by screen readers; usually its label.
